transcript:
HEADER: 2025-01-28 14:30 UTC | Duration 52m | Attendees: Alex Johnson (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Marta Ruiz (AtlasSearch Head of Search), Jun Park (ML Eng), Ravi Menon (Platform)

SUMMARY: quick recap at top: need POC to validate embeddings throughput and reranker latency, confirm which deployment mode (hosted/dedicated/private) meets compliance and perf.

TOPICS COVERED: embedding vector sizes, vector DB choices, hybrid search design, reranking model placement (inference on Redwood vs in-house), network egress and VPC constraints, SLA and pricing expectations.

-- TRANSCRIPT --
00:00 Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We got about 50 minutes, so we'll dig into what AtlasSearch is trying to validate for the embeddings plus rerank POC. Priya and I from Redwood; Marta, Jun, Ravi, you good?
00:12 Marta: Yep, thanks Alex. Morning for us — afternoon? — either way. Quick background: our search product mixes classic BM25 scoring with a neural reranker. We're evaluating moving the embedding generation and rerank inference off our in-house infra to something managed to reduce ops and lower tail latency.
00:30 Priya: Nice. Can you outline current qps, dataset sizes, and what your reranker looks like (model size, latency today)?
00:40 Jun: Sure. Currently we serve about 400 qps average, peaks up to 2k qps for short bursts. Docs about 200M documents total but POC will be on a ~10M subset. Embedding dim today is 768 from our in-house encoder; reranker is a distilled cross-encoder, ~220M params, tail p95 latency for rerank ~120ms when colocated with BM25 candidate fetch.
01:05 Alex: Helpful. So primary goals for the POC are: validate embedding throughput (generating vectors for documents and queries), vector DB integration (how Redwood outputs vectors or serves them), and rerank latency when the reranker model is hosted on Redwood vs run in your infra. Right?
01:17 Marta: Exactly. Also security — we'd need SOC 2 and SSO and potentially private VPC for production if perf looks good.
01:25 Priya: Understood. Quick clarifying q: when you say vector DB, are you planning to continue using AtlasSearch's own store, or moving to a third-party like Pinecone/Milvus?
01:33 Ravi: We'll keep AtlasSearch as the vector store for now — product is the DB. But we want Redwood to push embeddings back into our store or provide an API hook so we can pull them.
01:42 Priya: That's fine — Redwood can output embeddings as a batched export or stream via API. For live QPS we can also host the reranker and return scored results which you can ingest, depending on latency SLO.
01:53 Jun: On dimensionality — we're testing 768 vs 1024 for representational gains. Any throughput delta we should expect?
02:03 Priya: Yes, roughly linear in memory footprint. For generating embeddings, going from 768 to 1024 increases token-level compute and bandwidth; on a typical A100/RTX class GPU we see 30–40% higher latency per vector if model increases param size or embedding dim increases because of additional matrix ops. But batching helps a lot for throughput.
02:23 Alex: Important point: Redwood Recommend batching (we'll show sample batch sizes). For document-generation (offline indexing) you can push big batches — thousands — but for online query embeddings you want smaller batches to keep latency low.
02:34 Marta: What about hybrid search — we want to combine BM25 candidate fetch then embed+rerank. Our target end-to-end latency for user queries is <150ms p95. Is that realistic if the reranker is remote?
02:46 Priya: It's tight but possible. Two main components: network RTT to Redwood inference, and model latency. If reranker is small (220M) and you have warm instances and small batch concurrency, model infer can be ~40–80ms p95. Add 20–40ms network depending on region and VPC peering, plus BM25 fetch time. So you could reach ~120–150ms but it's sensitive.
03:10 Jun: If we keep reranker in our infra and only use Redwood for vector generation, it's simpler for latency, but we lose operational benefits. Also curious about throughput: if we need 2k QPS peak and each query triggers a rerank of 50 candidates, that's 100k rerank calls per second — unrealistic unless batch/rerank is more efficient.
03:32 Alex: Right — typical pattern is: BM25 fetch 100-200 candidates, compute embedding similarity to narrow to top K (say 50), then apply reranker only to top 10. Reranker is expensive; you shouldn't run it for the entire candidate set. We can help with candidate pruning strategies.
03:48 Marta: Ok that aligns. What about vector DB integration pattern — push vs pull vs streaming?
03:55 Priya: For indexing pipelines, push is easiest: Redwood returns batched embeddings (parquet/ndjson / direct S3 upload) which you then ingest. For live query embeddings, the flow is: query -> embed (Redwood) -> nearest neighbor search (Atlas DB) -> candidate ids -> reranker (Redwood or in-house). We can also host an endpoint that returns reranked results directly to your app if you prefer.
04:18 Ravi: Network & security question: if we used Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) would we need special firewall rules? Our security team insists on no public egress for PII workloads.
04:27 Priya: For Private mode we can offer a customer-managed VPC peering or private link. That avoids public egress and keeps traffic within your cloud region. We'll need a short network diagram and firewall ACLs.
04:37 Ravi: We'll share that. Also do you support KMS integration for embedding storage encryption?
04:42 Alex: Yes, Redwood Private supports KMS/HSM. Hosted can support encryption-at-rest but for customer-managed keys we recommend Private. We'll share SOC2 and tenant isolation docs.
04:52 Marta: Great. Can you give rough cost ballparks? We want to compare hosted token/embedding pricing vs dedicated reserved capacity.
04:57 Alex: High level: hosted is pay-as-you-go with per-embedding and per-inference token pricing; dedicated is monthly reserved GPU pools with predictable throughput — often more cost-effective at sustained high QPS. For 2k peak bursts, dedicated with autoscaling burst is common. We'll send sample numbers in the POC estimate.
05:15 Jun: One more perf nit: when you said batching helps — what batch sizes do you recommend for generating 10M doc vectors offline?
05:22 Priya: For offline indexing on gpus, we recommend batching 512–2048 vectors per step depending on memory. We'll provide a recommended config matrix for A100/RTX8000 and CPU-only fallbacks. For large-scale indexing you can use sharded parallel workers.
05:36 Marta: Regarding reranker model — if we increased capacity to a 700M or 1B reranker for quality, would Redwood support quantized int8 or int4 inference to reduce cost?
05:45 Priya: Yes, we support quantization-friendly execution paths. Int8 brings noticeable memory/latency wins; int4 is experimental for some architectures but available for certain models. We'll flag which model families are supported.
05:58 Jun: Latency when using int8 would change how much?
06:01 Priya: Typically 20–40% reduction in latency depending on kernel maturity. But you need to validate quality drop for reranker models, so we recommend running quality evals on your relevance set. Redwood Optimize can help with automated quantization recommendations and quality monitors.
06:20 Alex: Quick check — any legal/procurement timeline concerns? Marta?
06:24 Marta: Procurement prefers to see SOC2 and contract terms; estimated procurement lead time is 4–8 weeks for private deployment. For POC we'll try to stay on hosted or dedicated trial to avoid long procurement initially.
06:36 Ravi: If we do dedicated reserved capacity, how do rollouts and model version pinning work? We need a way to A/B test rerankers without disrupting search.
06:44 Priya: Redwood supports canary rollouts and A/B split at routing layer. You can pin certain customers or query buckets to model versions, and there's automatic fallback. We'll demo that in the deep technical session.
06:55 Alex: Good. Let's talk instrumentation — for the POC you'll want token/latency/cost breakdowns per route. Does Atlas already have metrics pipeline?
07:05 Jun: We have Prometheus + Grafana and can scrape Redwood-provided metrics; if you provide traces we can integrate into our dashboards.
07:13 Priya: Redwood exposes per-route metrics and tracing hooks; we can integrate via OTLP or push metrics; we'll share an example dashboard.
07:22 Marta: What's the expected turnaround for Redwood to run a small benchmark (we give 10k docs + 500 queries) and return p50/p95 runtimes and throughput?
07:30 Alex: If you provide the dataset and workload by Feb 7, we can run an initial benchmark and share results within 5 business days — so roughly Feb 14. That will include embedding gen times and reranker end-to-end latencies for the configured flow.
07:42 Jun: Sound good. A few edge-case Qs: what about cold-starts for rerank? How do you keep warm instances?
07:48 Priya: We keep warm pools, but cold starts can occur on scale events. For strict latency SLOs you should provision minimum instances or use dedicated. We'll document warm pool sizing heuristics.
07:59 Marta: Any documentation or bench spreadsheets we can look at?
08:02 Alex: We'll drop links: POC template, benchmark spreadsheet, SOC2 summary, network diagram template, sample reranker config. Links will be in follow-up email.
08:13 Jun: Great. Last question: hybrid search ranking — you mentioned fallback policies. If Redwood capacity momentarily drops, can we fallback to pure BM25 with approximate embeddings scoring locally?
08:23 Priya: Yes, you can define fallback policies — e.g., if model latency >250ms or error rate exceeds threshold, route to a lighter emb-only model or to BM25-only. We'll help set thresholds.
08:35 Marta: Thanks. That addresses most things. Recap for us: get POC template and pricing, we'll prep dataset and network constraints, and schedule the SE-led deep dive.
08:45 Alex: Perfect. We'll send items and aim to sync next week for scheduling. Thanks everyone.

END OF TRANSCRIPT
